explanation: The UK is a constitutional monarchy. The monarch is Head of State with a ceremonial role and must remain politically neutral.

angles.q: What kind of monarchy does the UK have?
alts: The UK system of government is described as what?
How is the UK's monarchy described?

tf.s: The monarch opens a new session of Parliament each year.
The monarch can refuse to sign any law passed by Parliament.
The monarch may advise, warn and encourage ministers in private.

explanation: The National Anthem of the UK is God Save the King, sung as God Save the Queen when the monarch is female.

angles.q: What is the UK's National Anthem?
alts: Which song is the National Anthem of the UK?

explanation: Members of the House of Lords are appointed, not elected. They include life peers, some hereditary peers and senior bishops.

angles.q: How are most members of the House of Lords chosen?
wrong: They are elected by the public
They are chosen by local councils
alts: Members of the House of Lords reach the chamber how?

tf.s: The House of Lords can delay a law passed by the Commons.
The House of Lords can permanently block any law.
Life peers cannot pass their title to their children.

explanation: A general election must be held at least every five years. If an MP dies or resigns, a by-election is held.

angles.q: How often must a general election be held at the latest?
alts: What is the maximum period between UK general elections?
General elections must take place at least how often?

angles.q: What is held when an MP resigns between general elections?
alts: If a seat in the Commons becomes vacant, what takes place?

tf.s: Voting in UK elections is by secret ballot.
You can apply for a postal vote if you cannot attend a polling station.

explanation: The Chancellor of the Exchequer runs the economy, the Home Secretary handles crime and immigration, and the Foreign Secretary manages relations abroad.

angles.q: Which minister is responsible for the economy?
alts: Who runs the UK economy in government?
The Treasury is led by which minister?

angles.q: Which minister is responsible for crime and policing?
alts: Policing and immigration fall to which minister?

angles.q: Which minister manages relations with other countries?
alts: Who is responsible for the UK's foreign relations?

multi.q: Which TWO of these are senior government ministers?

explanation: The Cabinet is a committee of about 20 senior ministers appointed by the Prime Minister, meeting weekly to decide government policy.

angles.q: About how many senior ministers sit in the Cabinet?
alts: The Cabinet is made up of roughly how many ministers?

tf.s: The Prime Minister chooses the members of the Cabinet.
The Opposition leader appoints a shadow cabinet.

explanation: The Speaker chairs debates in the Commons, keeps order and is politically neutral, though still an MP for a constituency.

angles.q: Who keeps order during debates in the House of Commons?
alts: Debates in the Commons are chaired by whom?

tf.s: The Speaker is elected by other MPs in a secret ballot.
The Speaker campaigns for their political party at elections.

explanation: Education, health, housing and social services are devolved. Defence, foreign affairs, immigration and national security are reserved to the UK government.

angles.q: Which of these is a devolved matter?
alts: Which policy area is controlled by the devolved administrations?

angles.q: Which of these remains with the UK government at Westminster?
alts: Which matter is reserved to the UK Parliament rather than devolved?

multi.q: Which TWO of these are reserved to the UK government?

explanation: Members of the Scottish Parliament are MSPs, and members of the Northern Ireland Assembly are MLAs.

angles.q: Members of the Northern Ireland Assembly are called what?
alts: What abbreviation is used for members of the Northern Ireland Assembly?

tf.s: The Scottish Parliament has 129 members.
The UK government can suspend the Northern Ireland Assembly.

explanation: County Courts deal with civil disputes, Crown Courts with serious crime, Magistrates' Courts with minor offences and Youth Courts with those aged 10 to 17.

angles.q: Which court deals with civil disputes such as debt and breach of contract?
alts: Debt and contract disputes are heard in which court?

angles.q: Which court deals with defendants aged 10 to 17 in England and Wales?
alts: Young people accused of crime appear in which court?

tf.s: The small claims procedure handles disputes over small sums of money.
In Scotland, the Children's Hearings System deals with most young offenders.

explanation: Judges interpret the law and ensure trials are fair. They are independent of government.

angles.q: What is the collective term for judges in the UK?
alts: Judges are collectively known as what?

tf.s: Judges in the UK are independent of the government.
Judges decide whether the government has acted within the law.

explanation: The police protect life and property, prevent disturbances and detect crime. They must obey the law themselves.

angles.q: What is the main duty of the police?
angles.a: To protect life and property and prevent crime
alts: The police in the UK are responsible for what?

tf.s: Complaints about the police can be made to an independent body.
The police may be corrupt without consequence.

explanation: Discrimination on grounds such as race, sex, religion, disability, age or sexual orientation is unlawful in the UK.

angles.q: Which of these is unlawful in the UK?
angles.a: Discriminating against someone because of their disability
wrong: Refusing service to a violent customer
alts: Which of these actions breaks UK equality law?

tf.s: Domestic violence is a serious crime in the UK.
Female genital mutilation is illegal in the UK.
Forced marriage is a criminal offence in the UK.
It is legal to take a girl abroad for female genital mutilation.

explanation: To vote you must be on the electoral register, which is updated each year by an annual canvass carried out by local councils.

angles.q: Who maintains the electoral register?
alts: Which body keeps the register of electors?

tf.s: The electoral register is updated each year.

explanation: MPs hold surgeries in their constituency so local people can discuss problems with them directly.

angles.q: What is an MP's surgery?
angles.a: A local meeting where constituents can raise problems
alts: Where can constituents meet their MP to discuss a problem?

tf.s: You can contact your MP by letter, email or telephone.
Members of the public can watch debates in Parliament from the public gallery.

explanation: Income tax funds government services. Most employees pay through PAYE, while self-employed people complete a self-assessment tax return.

angles.q: How do most employees pay income tax?
wrong: They do not pay income tax
alts: Income tax is normally collected from employees by which method?

tf.s: Self-employed people usually complete a self-assessment tax return.
National Insurance contributions are paid by almost everyone who works.

explanation: You must be 17 to drive a car, hold a valid licence, and have insurance. Vehicles over three years old need an annual MOT.

angles.q: What is the minimum age to drive a car in the UK?
alts: You must be at least how old to drive a car in the UK?

tf.s: Driving without valid insurance is a criminal offence.
Vehicles over three years old must pass an annual MOT test.

explanation: Ways of contributing include volunteering, becoming a school governor, helping at a local charity and looking after the environment.

angles.q: In Scotland, what is the equivalent of a school governor?
angles.a: A member of the parent council or school board
alts: Parents in Scotland can serve on which school body?

tf.s: Volunteering is a way of taking part in community life.
Recycling household waste helps protect the environment.

explanation: Newspapers may support a political party, but broadcasters must give balanced coverage of rival viewpoints, especially during elections.

angles.q: Which of these must be politically balanced by law?
alts: Who is legally required to give balanced political coverage in the UK?

tf.s: UK newspapers are allowed to support a political party.
Hansard is the official record of proceedings in Parliament.

explanation: Pressure and lobby groups try to influence government policy on particular issues and play an important part in public debate.

angles.q: What do pressure groups try to do?
alts: The purpose of a lobby group is to do what?
